<SPAN 11>For good and valuable consideration, the receipt and sufficiency of which are hereby acknowledged, the Parties hereto agree as follows:</SPAN 11>
<SPAN 12>1. Purpose. </SPAN 12><SPAN 13>The Company and Third Party wish to discuss a potential business opportunity under which each may disclose its Confidential Information to the other.</SPAN 13>
<SPAN 14>2. Definition. </SPAN 14><SPAN 15>“Confidential Information” means any information, technical data or know-how, including, but not limited to, that which relates to research, products, services, customers, markets, software, developments, inventions, processes, designs, drawings, engineering, marketing or finances, disclosed orally or in written or electronic form, and which is marked or identified by the disclosing party as “proprietary” or “confidential”. </SPAN 15><SPAN 16>Confidential Information does not include information, technical data or know-how that:</SPAN 16>
<SPAN 17>(i) is in the possession of the receiving party at the time of disclosure as shown by the receiving partyʼs files and records immediately prior to the time of disclosure; or</SPAN 17>
<SPAN 18>(ii) prior or after the time of disclosure becomes part of the public knowledge or literature, not as a result of any inaction or action of the receiving party;</SPAN 18>
<SPAN 19>(iii) is approved for release by the disclosing party; or</SPAN 19>
<SPAN 20>(iv) is independently developed by the receiving party without the use of any Confidential Information of the other party.</SPAN 20>
<SPAN 21>3. Non-disclosure of Confidential Information. </SPAN 21><SPAN 22>The Company and Third Party each agree not to use the Confidential Information disclosed to it by the other party for its own use or for any purpose except to carry out discussions concerning and the undertaking of any business relationship between the two. </SPAN 22><SPAN 23>The recipient of Confidential Information will not disclose such Confidential Information to anyone, including to their employees; however, the recipient of Confidential Information may disclose such information to certain employees who are required to have such information to carry out the contemplated business. </SPAN 23><SPAN 24>Each has had or will have employees to whom Confidential Information of the other is disclosed sign a Non-disclosure Agreement in content substantially similar to this Agreement and will notify the other in writing of the names of the persons who have had access to Confidential Information of the other party. </SPAN 24><SPAN 25>Each agrees that it will take all reasonable steps to protect the secrecy of and avoid disclosure or use of Confidential Information of the other in order to prevent it from falling into the public domain or the possession of unauthorised persons. </SPAN 25><SPAN 26>Each agrees to notify the other in writing of any misuse or misappropriation of Confidential Information of the other that may come to its attention.</SPAN 26>
<SPAN 27>4. Ownership. </SPAN 27><SPAN 28>All Confidential Information shall remain the exclusive property of Disclosing Party, and Recipient shall have no right to use Confidential Information except as provided herein. </SPAN 28><SPAN 29>No patent, copyright, trademark or other proprietary right or licence is conveyed by this Agreement with respect to Confidential Information.</SPAN 29>
<SPAN 30>5. Return of Materials. </SPAN 30><SPAN 31>Any materials or documents that have been furnished by one party to the other will be promptly returned, accompanied by all copies of such documentation, after the business possibility has been rejected or concluded.</SPAN 31>
<SPAN 32>6. Intellectual Property Rights. </SPAN 32><SPAN 33>Nothing in this Agreement is intended to grant any rights under any patent or copyright of either party, nor shall this Agreement grant either party any rights in or to the other partyʼs Confidential Information, except the limited right to review such Confidential Information solely for the purposes of determining whether to enter into the proposed business relationship between the parties and in carrying out such relationship. </SPAN 33><SPAN 34>The disclosing party warrants that it has the right to disclose its Confidential Information to the receiving party. </SPAN 34><SPAN 35>Otherwise, all information is provided “as is” and without any warranty, express, implied or otherwise, regarding its accuracy or performance.</SPAN 35>
<SPAN 36>7. <SPAN 39>8. Term. </SPAN 39><SPAN 40>This Agreement may be terminated at all times with a 30 daysʼ prior written notice provided, however, that the confidentiality obligations herein shall terminate </SPAN 40><SPAN 41>____________ years following the date of termination of this Agreement.</SPAN 41>
<SPAN 42>9. Miscellaneous. </SPAN 42><SPAN 43>This Agreement shall be binding upon and for the benefit of the undersigned parties, their successors and assigns provided that Confidential Information may not be assigned without consent of the disclosing party. </SPAN 43><SPAN 44>Failure to enforce any provision of this Agreement shall not constitute a waiver of any term hereof. </SPAN 44><SPAN 45>This Agreement shall be governed by and construed and enforced in accordance with the laws of the State/Territory </SPAN 45><SPAN 46>____________________________________________ </SPAN 46><SPAN 47>as they apply to contracts entered into and wholly to be performed in the State/Territory of </SPAN 47><SPAN 48>_______________________________________. </SPAN 48><SPAN 49>The Federal and State courts within the State/Territory of </SPAN 49><SPAN 50>_________________________________________ </SPAN 50><SPAN 51>shall have exclusive jurisdiction to adjudicate any dispute arising out of this Agreement.</SPAN 51>
<SPAN 52>10. Remedies. </SPAN 52><SPAN 53>Each party agrees that its obligations hereunder are necessary and reasonable in order to protect the other party and the other partyʼs business, and expressly agrees that monetary damages would be inadequate to compensate the other party for any breach of any covenant or agreement set forth herein. </SPAN 53><SPAN 54>Accordingly, each party agrees and acknowledges that any such violation or threatened violation will cause irreparable injury to the other party and that, in addition to any other remedies that may be available, in law, at equity or otherwise, the other party shall be entitled to obtain injunctive relief against the threatened breach of the Agreement or the continuation of any such breach, without the necessity of proving actual damages.</SPAN 54>
<SPAN 55>11. guidance.when: The source expressly makes return or destruction of protected information operative upon termination, expiration, rejection, or conclusion of the agreement, project, or contemplated relationship.
guidance.inspection: Separate the operative return or destruction duty from request-only duties, then verify that the stated trigger is an ending event and carry forward any scope limits or exceptions.
guidance.evidence_requirement: Cite the ending-event trigger together with the operative return or destruction language; include a governing list introduction when the duty is an item.

guidance.when: The source expressly exempts identified copies or stored protected information from a return or deletion duty and permits their continued retention.
guidance.inspection: Read the general return or destruction rule with every overriding exception; identify what may remain, who or what system may hold it, its purpose, and continuing restrictions.
guidance.evidence_requirement: Cite the retention permission and any governing exception transition, plus material limits such as archival-only access, dispute purpose, or continuing confidentiality.

guidance.when: The source expressly prohibits disclosure of the existence or occurrence of negotiations, discussions, an agreement in progress, receipt of evaluation material, or terms or status of the contemplated transaction.
guidance.inspection: Distinguish secrecy of the deal process or agreement facts from ordinary secrecy of confidential information, and preserve consent, audience, and publicity qualifications.
guidance.evidence_requirement: Cite the prohibition's governing language and each relied-on enumerated subject; a generic nondisclosure clause alone is insufficient.

guidance.when: A source clause expressly addresses making, reproducing, automatically creating, returning, destroying, or retaining copies of protected information.
guidance.inspection: Classify the copy language by legal function: affirmative exception, automatic-copy acknowledgement, consent-conditioned prohibition, mere reference to existing copies, return duty, or retention carve-out. Do not infer creation permission from employee access or generic safeguarding.
guidance.evidence_requirement: Cite the operative copy wording and its governing condition or exception; read adjacent retention or return language when it changes the clause's function.

guidance.when: The source expressly states that the agreement or disclosure grants, conveys, or confers no right or license in protected information or associated intellectual property.
guidance.inspection: Identify the denied grant separately from ownership, limited-purpose use, and review permissions; preserve any express narrow exception without treating it as a general license.
guidance.evidence_requirement: Cite the operative no-rights or no-license wording and any material exception; ownership language may be retained as independent support but is not a substitute for an express grant denial.

guidance.when: The source expressly limits use of protected information to a stated agreement, transaction, evaluation, project, discussion, or business-relationship purpose, whether phrased as 'only' or as a prohibition with a necessary-purpose exception.
guidance.inspection: Treat the permitted purpose as the boundary of the restriction, not as permission for unrelated uses; capture both affirmative only-use wording and complementary other-purpose prohibitions.
guidance.evidence_requirement: Cite the operative use limitation and the text identifying the permitted purpose; include a governing introduction when the rule is listed.
